question.worked_solution:
Here, we have the product of two functions $u(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡x$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{cosh}⁡{x}^{2}.$ So, we apply the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{′}\cdot \operatorname{cosh}⁡{x}^{2}+\operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot (\operatorname{cosh}⁡{x}^{2})^{′} \\  & =\frac{1}{x}\cdot \operatorname{cosh}⁡{x}^{2}+\operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot 2x\operatorname{sinh}⁡{x}^{2} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cosh}⁡{x}^{2}}{x}+2x\operatorname{ln}⁡x\operatorname{sinh}⁡{x}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{x}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡{x}^{2}+2{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\operatorname{sinh}⁡{x}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$
